architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the combined modifier intervention as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 across at least two repeats is <3.80%, with every individual repeat also <7.61%. The 3.80% threshold is below half the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If the mean SI_15_60 is >=7.61%, falsify H-RESIN and contradict the low-drift prediction of H-DUAL for the active dual-axis composition; H-CORE remains consistent with the result. If the mean is <3.80%, falsify H-CORE at the registered resolution. A mean from 3.80% through <7.61% is non-decisive and falsifies neither hypothesis at the prespecified thresholds.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run an acrylic-only 120 C matched-window thermal hold at 15% acrylic-like modifier with the corresponding reactive-core fraction and at least two independent repeats, using the same 15, 30, 45 and 60 min sampling, to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = ((eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15) × 100, reported as the mean percent drift across at least two independent preparation repeats, with individual repeat values also reported.
judge_normalized.rationale: This experiment directly measures the unresolved 120 C isothermal drift coordinate and tests the combined intervention against the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. S1C41 is inside the supported modifier region, minimizes departure from the characterized E2 reactive core among the deterministic top-tied cards, and is intended to mitigate the established viscosity-growth failure. Its result can separate H-CORE from the combined low-drift alternatives, but cannot attribute suppression to the acrylic-like axis, the minor tackifier-like axis, or their interaction.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120. The Skeptic's objection that the dual-axis composition cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL is valid and is retained explicitly as an unresolved hypothesis pair; it does not make another tied candidate preferable because all five tied candidates share that entanglement. The tie was broken in favor of S1C41 because it uses the smallest acrylic loading and smallest supported total modifier burden while retaining both independently supported axes. I also adopted the Skeptic's recommendation to adjudicate thresholds on the repeat mean while reporting individual repeats.

planner.failure_mode: Time-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged residence of the 120 C melt, with the contribution of modifier chemistry versus simple reactive-material dilution unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal holds show a 15-60 min relative viscosity change of 51.54% for E5 versus 9.51% for E1, establishing substantial formulation-dependent isothermal drift.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local time-coordinate evidence contains only two original formulations, each with one 120 C hold and four time points from 15 to 90 min. There are no repeated hold trajectories for modified compositions, so the magnitude and shape of drift in the candidate modifier space are less resolved than the temperature response, which has multiple 80-130 C sweeps, or the viscosity level, for which matched-temperature repeat spread is at least directly observed.
measurement_requirements: Measure a matched-window 120 C thermal hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 as the primary observable.
Use at least two independent preparation repeats for each tested composition and record complete preparation and thermal-history information.

Include compositions that separately activate the acrylic-like axis and the minor tackifier-like axis, while controlling or explicitly reporting reactive mass fraction so the result can be compared with the E1-derived linear-dilution prediction.
Report both the isothermal drift trajectory and the realized viscosity level at the hold-window endpoints so drift is not confounded with an unmeasured viscosity-scale displacement.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and a matched 120 C hold window, does modifier addition reduce viscosity drift only according to linear reactive-core dilution (H-CORE), suppress it substantially beyond dilution through resin modification (H-RESIN), or require a nonzero minor tackifier axis while acrylic addition alone mainly changes the realized viscosity level (H-DUAL)?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL: both predict low drift for this dual-axis composition

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, drift is below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. This falsifies H-CORE at the stated resolution and supports H-RESIN over H-CORE. Because both modifier axes are active, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction; the high-drift result also contradicts H-DUAL's expectation of low drift when the minor tackifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% is not decisive at the registered resolution: it would support neither the specified superlinear-suppression threshold nor a clear linear-dilution outcome. It would leave H-CORE, H-RESIN and H-DUAL incompletely adjudicated, with H-RESIN versus H-DUAL still unresolved regardless.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly from the 15 and 60 min viscosities during the 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses a higher 17.5% acrylic loading and therefore a larger modifier burden without separating any additional registered hypothesis pair.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses 20% acrylic rather than the minimum directly supported 15% level, increasing departure from the E2 core without additional discrimination.
It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses 22.5% acrylic and a larger intervention than necessary for the same two separable hypothesis pairs.

It is genuinely tied in deterministic VOI, but uses the largest 25% acrylic loading in the supported region, creating the greatest modifier burden without improving direct observability or hypothesis separation.

proposer.reasoning: The failure mode is directly isothermal drift, and M-HOLD-120 measures that quantity without model fitting or extrapolation. S1C41 activates both independently supported modifier axes at 15% acrylic and 5% minor tackifier, has zero extrapolation risk, and separates H-CORE from both alternative mechanisms at a 2.00% resolution threshold. Its limitation is structural: the dual-axis composition cannot distinguish resin-wide suppression from tackifier-required suppression, so an acrylic-only follow-up would be required for H-RESIN versus H-DUAL.
proposer.tie_break_justification: The deterministic layer reports genuine indifference among these five cards: they have identical component vectors and VOI scores. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest acrylic loading and therefore the smallest supported total modifier burden while remaining inside the directly supported acrylic region and the repeatedly documented approximately 5% minor-tackifier region. It is the least departure from the characterized E2 reactive core among the tied cards.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved without an acrylic-only 120 C hold.
The combined modifier intervention does not permit attribution to the acrylic-like axis, minor-tackifier-like axis, or their interaction.
Reactive-core dilution is used as the H-CORE comparison, so the result remains conditional on the registered linear-dilution prediction.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state; preparation and thermal-history variation may confound threshold crossings.
The protocol does not specify whether thresholds apply to every repeat, the repeat mean, or an uncertainty interval.
Endpoint viscosity levels and realization-specific viscosity-scale displacement may complicate interpretation of SI_15_60.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 simultaneously changes the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes and lowers the reactive mass fraction to 0.8000, so a low drift result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute the effect to one axis. However, this entanglement is explicitly declared, and the proposed matched-window hold remains the most direct experiment for separating H-CORE from the combined alternative mechanisms. The objection therefore limits the formulation-level interpretation and requires an acrylic-only follow-up, with prespecified repeat aggregation and uncertainty rules; it does not make another member of the tied set preferable. The tie does not resolve this issue because all five tied experiments leave the same hypothesis pair entangled.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the five-way tied top set. No re-weighting in the 25-scenario sweep changed the tied top set, and every recommendation_flip_boundary term survives the full 0.5x-1.5x sweep. Thus no tested perturbation makes the proposal cease to be top ranked. The base weights are scientifically defensible because they emphasize direct measurement of the declared failure mode, hypothesis discrimination, and uncertainty reduction; the small base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower of 0.004583 still warrants retaining the tie rather than treating the ranking as decisive.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The numerical criteria are attainable because SI_15_60 is measured directly at 15 and 60 minutes, and the S1C41 thresholds of 3.804% and 7.608% are separated by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. Attainability is weakened by the absence of a rule defining how the two repeats are aggregated and by uncontrolled process-state variation, so the protocol can generate the required measurements but does not fully specify reproducible threshold adjudication.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could not support the specific claim that the minor tackifier axis is required, nor could it uniquely establish H-RESIN.
objections.objection: The proposed composition S1C41 contains both 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100. Its predicted SI_15_60 values are identical for H-RESIN and H-DUAL (3.804%), so the experiment cannot distinguish resin-wide suppression from tackifier-required suppression. The proposer explicitly declares this entanglement, but therefore the claim is limited to separating H-CORE from the combined alternative, not adjudicating all three hypotheses.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any attribution to acrylic-driven viscosity relocation, tackifier-driven drift suppression, or a unique resin mechanism would be unsupported; only comparison of the combined intervention against the registered dilution prediction is available.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously and replaces 20% of the reactive-core mass with 15% acrylic-like modifier plus 5% minor tackifier-like modifier. The resulting SI_15_60 change can therefore not be attributed to AC1920, TK100, or an interaction between them. In addition, the proposed experiment changes reactive mass fraction to 0.8000, making the comparison depend on the H-CORE linear-dilution assumption rather than isolating a single modifier mechanism.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift result could be interpreted as a formulation effect when part of the difference reflects an uncontrolled preparation or state displacement. The directness of SI_15_60 does not by itself establish formulation-level causality.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly calculated from measured 15 and 60 minute viscosities, with no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This attack surface is largely satisfied. However, SI_15_60 alone does not control for a realization-specific viscosity-scale displacement, despite the measurement requirements requesting endpoint viscosity levels.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The stated falsification of H-RESIN at SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, or of H-CORE below 3.80%, could become an arbitrary post hoc decision rather than a reproducible falsification rule.
objections.objection: The thresholds are numerically separable from the declared 2.00% resolution: for S1C41, H-CORE predicts 7.608% and the low-drift criterion is 3.804%, a 3.804 percentage-point gap. However, the protocol says only 'across at least two repeats' and does not define whether the threshold applies to every repeat, the mean, or a prespecified uncertainty interval. Thus a result near 7.61% cannot be adjudicated reproducibly under the stated repeat protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A threshold-crossing result could falsely falsify H-CORE or H-RESIN because of uncontrolled preparation or hold-history variation.
objections.objection: M-HOLD-120 has process_state_risk score 0.75, does not control process state, and identifies six missing process fields. Two independent preparations may therefore differ in thermal and preparation history by an amount that is not quantified for the modified composition. The criterion can produce numerical SI values, but the protocol does not establish that a threshold crossing is due to composition rather than realization state.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological result would be overstated as molecular mechanistic evidence rather than evidence consistent with a formulation-level suppression hypothesis.
objections.objection: The proposal appropriately treats H-RESIN and H-DUAL as formulation-level rheological hypotheses, and M-HOLD-120 cannot establish a molecular reaction pathway. Any interpretation of the low drift as proof of a molecular 'encounter frequency' mechanism would exceed the registered claim boundary, although the proposer does not explicitly make that stronger claim.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an acrylic-only 120 C hold at the same acrylic loading and matched reactive-core proportions, alongside the dual-axis S1C41 hold, and prespecify that thresholds apply to the repeat mean with an uncertainty rule. Record and standardize all preparation and thermal-history fields and report eta_15 and eta_60 in addition to SI_15_60.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The S1C41 composition activates both modifier axes simultaneously while also reducing the reactive mass fraction to 0.8000, so the experiment cannot attribute any observed drift change to either axis or their interaction. It can only compare the combined intervention with the H-CORE dilution prediction; a low result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
